newsitem.title: INDIA: India to allow firms to set-up own pension plans.
newsitem.headline: India to allow firms to set-up own pension plans.

text.p: India will allow companies to develop their own pension schemes for their employees, the chairman of the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) said on Tuesday.

"We have permitted file and use pension plans, which will allow a corporation to make its own pension plan and start using it, as long as it conforms to the laws of the land," N Rangachary, chairman, IRA said while addressing a seminar organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce.
He said as long as the plan is ratified by an actuary a company can start using the plan as soon as it is framed.

Rangachary stressed the need for appropriate reforms in provident, pension and insurance funds to take care of a rapidly aging population and provide big funds for infrastructure development in the country.

He said an expert group of the Finance Ministry had estimated the total infrastructure investment needed in India over the next five years to be between $115 billion to $130 billion, and 85 percent of this will have to be domestically financed.
The population of old people is growing at a rapid pace, he said. "By 2005, it is estimated that 60 percent of the population would be above the age of 60 years."

To increase the effectiveness of pension funds, Rangachary said an environment has to be created where more funds can develop and more products developed to cater to the needs of the different segments of society, he said.

Rangachary said there was a need to make pension and insurance products cheaper to encompass all sections of Indian society, particularly the rural segment, which is growing in affluence and its contribution to the economic growth of the country.
